title: Dry to sweet
subtitle: Riesling's full range
objectives: Explain the balance of sugar and acidity

steps.title: Dry and off-dry
steps.body: Dry Riesling, from Alsace, Austria, Australia and Germany's trocken and GG wines, is crisp and mineral, with citrus and stone fruit. Off-dry Riesling, like many Mosel Kabinetts, balances a little sugar with high acidity, often at only 7.5 to 9% alcohol, tasting fresh rather than sweet.

steps.title: Sugar and acidity
steps.body: The balance between sugar and acidity defines Riesling. High acidity, often 8 to 10 g/l, makes even 40 or 50 g/l of sugar taste only slightly sweet. The International Riesling Foundation created a taste profile scale, from dry to sweet, that some producers print on the back label to help buyers.

steps.prompt: Why does an off-dry Mosel Kabinett taste fresh rather than sweet?
steps.explanation: Acidity counters the perception of sweetness.

steps.title: Sweet Riesling
steps.body: Auslese, Beerenauslese, Eiswein and Trockenbeerenauslese are sweet, sometimes extremely so: TBA can exceed 300 g/l of sugar, with only 6 to 8% alcohol. Riesling's acidity keeps them lively. These are among the longest-lived wines in the world.

steps.prompt: Which Riesling styles are usually dry?
steps.explanation: TBA is among the sweetest wines in the world.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Riesling ranges from bone dry to intensely sweet
High acidity balances sugar, making off-dry wines taste fresh
Sweet Riesling can exceed 300 g/l and live for decades
